papers.title: Separate Bombs from Firecrackers: Intention-guided Vulnerability Assessment via LLM
papers.abstract: 用静态分析加 LLM 从漏洞代码抽取攻击意图，再以强化学习 prompt-tuning 做无需人工描述的漏洞严重度评估，对象是传统软件源码。

papers.title: No More Hidden Pitfalls? Exposing Smart Contract Bad Practices with LLM-Powered Hybrid Analysis
papers.abstract: 提出 SCALM：用 LLM 做函数级切片与多层语义推理，检测以太坊智能合约不良实践，对象是 Solidity。

papers.title: A Unified Framework for Function-Level Vulnerability Detection and Explanation in Smart Contracts
papers.abstract: 用层次交叉注意力子图网络在函数级定位智能合约漏洞，再用 LLM 生成类型、根因与修复说明。

papers.title: From Component Snapshots to Lifecycle Traces: Agent-Based Software Composition Analysis
papers.abstract: 用 agent 贯穿代码到运行时各阶段重建组件生命周期轨迹，评估 Java/JS/Python 供应链漏洞暴露。

papers.title: (Don't) Trust, but (Don't) Verify: Developers' Attention to Security in AI-Generated Code
papers.abstract: 人工智能编码助手正在迅速改变软件开发，但众所周知会产生不安全的代码。之前的工作已经衡量了人工智能辅助开发人员是否生成了安全的代码，但人们对他们如何评估人工智能生成的代码知之甚少：他们是否能够识别漏洞、他们使用什么线索以及信任如何影响他们的决策。无论是使用自动完成、聊天工具还是人工智能代理，此评估步骤都是确保人工智能开发安全的基础。作为第一步，我们对 100 名参与者进行了远程观察研究，隔离了这个评估阶段。参与者的任务是为四个 C 链表任务生成安全且功能性的代码。对于每一项，参与者都能够循环浏览人工智能生成的五种安全性和功能各异的建议，选择一项，然后将他们的选择编辑为最终提交。参与者还完成了一项关于他们的决策和对人工智能生成代码安全性的看法的研究后调查，23 名参与者完成了更深入的访谈。
papers.abstractEn: AI coding assistants are rapidly transforming software development, but are known to produce insecure code. Prior work has measured whether AI-assisted developers produce secure code, but less is known about how they evaluate AI-generated code: whether they can identify vulnerabilities, what cues they use, and how trust shapes their decisions. This evaluation step is foundational to secure development with AI, whether using auto-complete, chat tools, or AI agents. As a first step, we conducted a remote observational study with 100 participants isolating this evaluation stage. Participants were tasked with producing secure and functional code for four C linked-list tasks. For each, participants were able to cycle through five AI-generated suggestions varying in security and functionality, select one, and edit their choice into a final submission. Participants also completed a post-study survey about their decision-making and perception of AI-generated code's security and 23 completed a more in-depth interview.

papers.title: Bug Whisperer: Unleashing LLMs to Craft Context-Aware Tests Guided by Path Constraints and Bug Clues
papers.abstract: 使用大型语言模型 (LLM) 的自动单元测试生成因其简化软件测试的潜力而受到广泛关注。尽管前景广阔，但现有方法往往无法有效检测错误。 LLM 生成的测试的错误检测能力有两个关键限制：（1）他们很难识别和关注大型复杂代码库中与错误相关的信息，特别是当错误嵌入在复杂的程序依赖项和嵌套条件中时。 (2) 当在没有更多上下文的情况下提供焦点方法时，现有的基于 LLM 的方法在生成正确的测试用例方面效果较差。为了应对这些挑战，我们提出了 BugWhisper，这是一种包含三个核心模块的新颖方法：错​​误检测和定位模块、路径约束构建模块和测试生成模块。在错误检测和定位模块中，我们利用定制设计的提示从法学硕士中提取并突出显示错误信息。路径约束构建模块引入了基于贪婪的路径提取算法，以优先考虑覆盖最大数量的错误语句的错误触发路径。然后使用来自这些路径的约束来生成路径条件约束提示。最后，测试生成模块通过将路径约束与多种类型的上下文信息（包括导入上下文、类类型上下文、焦点类方法上下文和错误语句信息）集成来构造上下文感知提示。这些丰富的提示指导法学硕士生成更有效、更精确的测试用例。我们对 Defects4J 基准测试的评估表明，BugWhisper 增强了法学硕士的错误检测能力。具体来说，与现有的state-of-the-art基线相比，其编译通过率提高了78.02%，bug成功检测率提高了133.33%。此外，BugWhisper 将线路和分支覆盖率分别提高了 8.36% 和 15.89%。消融研究进一步验证了每个提示组件的贡献，凸显了 BugWhisper 作为复杂软件系统中错误检测的系统且高效的解决方案的潜力。
papers.abstractEn: Automated unit test generation using Large Language Models (LLMs) has garnered significant attention due to its potential to streamline software testing. Despite its promise, existing approaches often fall short in effectively detecting bugs. There are two key limitations in the bug detection capabilities of tests generated by LLMs: (1) It is difficult for them to identify and focus on bug-related information within large and complex codebases, particularly when bugs are embedded in intricate program dependencies and nested conditions. (2) Existing LLM-based methods are less effective in generating correct test cases when the focal method is provided without more context. To address these challenges, we propose BugWhisper, a novel approach comprising three core modules: bug detection & localization module, path constraint construction module, and test generation module. In the bug detection & localization module, we leverage custom-designed prompts to extract and highlight buggy information from LLMs. The path constraint construction module introduces a greedy-based path extraction algorithm to prioritize bug-triggering paths that cover the maximum number of buggy statements. Constraints from these paths are then used to generate path condition constraint prompts. Finally, the test generation module constructs context-aware prompts by integrating path constraints with multiple types of context information, including import context, class type context, focal class method context, and buggy statement information. These enriched prompts guide LLMs to generate more effective and precise test cases. Our evaluation on the Defects4J benchmark demonstrates that BugWhisper enhances the bug detection capabilities of LLMs. Specifically, compared with existing state-of-the-art baselines, it achieves a 78.02% improvement in compilation passing rate, and a 133.33% boost in the bug successful detection rate. Besides, BugWhisper improves line and branch coverage by 8.36% and 15.89%, respectively. Ablation studies further validate the contribution of each prompt component, highlighting BugWhisper's potential as a systematic and efficient solution for bug detection in complex software systems.

papers.title: Testing like Mad Libs: Fuzzing SMT Solvers with Historical Unusual Inputs Empowered by LLMs
papers.abstract: 确保可满足性模理论 (SMT) 求解器的正确性至关重要，因为它是广泛的关键软件工程实践的基石。因此，人们提出了各种方法来测试 SMT 求解器，包括利用大型语言模型 (LLM) 生成 SMT 求解器模糊测试输入公式的最新进展。然而，直接使用LLM来制作SMT公式会导致大量无效输入。此外，我们最近的研究证明了使用历史错误触发输入来指导测试公式生成的有效性，因为这些输入有助于锻炼求解器的深层状态。基于这些见解，我们提出了 MadFuzz，这是一种增强的方法，利用法学硕士的能力，通过完成历史错误触发输入的框架来巧妙地综合测试公式。此外，MadFuzz 还结合了基于求解器行为的反馈机制，其中包括 LLM 引导的提示优化和基于采样的种子输入选择。为了评估 MadFuzz 的有效性，我们使用三种尖端的 SMT 求解器：Z3、cvc5 和 Bitwuzla 进行了全面评估。我们的结果表明，MadFuzz 已在求解器中识别出 20 个已确认的真实错误，其中 19 个已被开发人员解决。此外，我们的实验表明，MadFuzz 在代码覆盖率和错误检测能力方面超越了现有的 SMT 求解器模糊器。
papers.abstractEn: Ensuring the correctness of Satisfiability Modulo Theory (SMT) solvers is of paramount importance, as it serves as the cornerstone of a broad spectrum of critical software engineering practices. Consequently, various methodologies have been proposed to test SMT solvers, including recent advances that utilize Large Language Models (LLMs) to generate input formulas for SMT solver fuzzing. However, directly employing LLMs to craft SMT formulas will result in an abundance of invalid inputs. Furthermore, our recent study demonstrated the effectiveness of using historical bug-triggering inputs to guide the generation of test formulas, as these inputs help exercise solvers’ deep states. Building on these insights, we present MadFuzz , an enhanced approach that leverages the capabilities of LLMs to ingeniously synthesize test formulas by completing the skeletons of historical bug-triggering inputs. Moreover, MadFuzz incorporates a feedback mechanism based on solvers’ behavior, which consists of LLM-guided prompt optimization and sampling-based seed input selection. To evaluate the effectiveness of MadFuzz , we conducted a comprehensive assessment using three cutting-edge SMT solvers: Z3, cvc5, and Bitwuzla. Our results demonstrate that MadFuzz has identified 20 confirmed real bugs in the solvers, 19 of which have already been addressed by developers. Additionally, our experiments demonstrate that MadFuzz surpasses existing SMT solver fuzzers in code coverage and bug detection capability.

papers.title: SPDZCoder: Combining Expert Knowledge with LLMs for Generating Privacy-Computing Code
papers.abstract: 隐私计算受到越来越多的关注，但由于库函数有限，需要从头开始实现功能，以及数据遗忘的要求，编写隐私计算代码对开发人员来说仍然是一个挑战，与程序员的直觉思维和惯例相矛盾。使用大型语言模型（LLM）自动生成隐私计算代码可以简化开发工作并降低使用隐私计算框架的障碍，因为LLM在编码任务方面表现出强大的能力。然而，由于有效预训练或微调所需的 MP-SPDZ 数据稀缺，现有的法学硕士在隐私保护计算的代码翻译方面仍然面临挑战，例如将 Python 翻译为 MP-SPDZ。此外，缺乏基准进一步阻碍了翻译质量的评估。为了解决这些限制，这项工作提出了 SPDZCoder，这是一种免培训框架，它将法学硕士与专家知识相结合，用于生成隐私计算代码。具体来说，SPDZCoder采用严格的程序收集高质量的专家知识来表示Python和MP-SPDZ之间语义表达的差异，并基于这些知识推导将Python翻译成MP-SPDZ的转换规则。然后，SPDZCoder 在三阶段管道中使用转换规则逐步将 Python 代码转换为 MP-SPDZ 代码。为了评估 SPDZCoder，我们手动构建了一个基准数据集 SPDZEval，它包含六个数据分割，每个数据分割代表 MP-SPDZ 实现中一类不同的挑战性任务。大量实验表明，SPDZCoder 实现了卓越的性能，显着超过了 pass@1 和 pass@2 的基线。具体来说，以 GPT-4 作为主干的 SPDZCoder 在 pass@1 和 pass@2 中分别获得了 \(85.94\%\) 和 \(92.01\%\) 的总体正确率值，而性能最佳的基线分别仅达到 \(63.58\%\) 和 \(76.36\%\) 。
papers.abstractEn: Privacy computing receives increasing attention but writing privacy computing code remains challenging for developers due to limited library functions, necessitating function implementation from scratch, and data-obliviousness requirement, contradicting intuitive thinking and usual practices of programmers. Automating the generation of privacy computing code with large language models (LLMs) can streamline development effort and lower the barrier to using privacy computing frameworks since LLMs exhibit strong capabilities in coding tasks. However, existing LLMs still encounter challenges in code translation for privacy-preserving computation—such as translating Python to MP-SPDZ—due to the scarcity of MP-SPDZ data required for effective pre-training or fine-tuning. Moreover, the lack of benchmark further hinders the evaluation of translation quality. To address the limitations, this work proposes SPDZCoder, a training-free framework that combines LLMs with expert knowledge for generating privacy computing code. Specifically, SPDZCoder employs a rigorous procedure for collecting high-quality expert knowledge to represent the semantic-expressing differences between Python and MP-SPDZ, and derives transformation rules for translating Python to MP-SPDZ based on these knowledge. Then, SPDZCoder progressively converts Python code into MP-SPDZ code using transformation rules in a three-stage pipeline. To evaluate SPDZCoder, we manually constructed a benchmark dataset, SPDZEval, which comprises six data splits, each representing a distinct class of challenging tasks in MP-SPDZ implementation. Extensive experiments demonstrate that SPDZCoder achieves superior performance, significantly surpassing baselines in pass@1 and pass@2. Specifically, SPDZCoder with GPT-4 as its backbone attains overall correctness values of \(85.94\%\) and \(92.01\%\) in pass@1 and pass@2, respectively, whereas the best-performing baseline achieves only \(63.58\%\) and \(76.36\%\) , respectively.

papers.title: CESBench: Benchmarking Large Language Models on Cryptographic Engineering Security for IoT Devices
papers.abstract: 对于物联网 (IoT) 设备，仅靠安全算法是不够的：具有物理访问权限的攻击者可以直接攻击实现，而且其缺陷一旦部署就很难修复。大型语言模型 (LLM) 现在用于构建和分析此类实现。 LLM 基准针对密码学和一般网络安全，但没有涵盖密码工程。在本文中，我们展示了 CESBench，涵盖物联网设备加密工程安全六个子领域的 380 个专家撰写的项目：侧通道、故障注入、实施、对策、评估和集成。四种任务类型针对不同的能力：209个多项选择项测试回忆，67个判断项需要安全判决及其理由，63个场景项需要工程诊断，41个代码任务由572个测试用例评分。为了验证基准，11 位开放式和专有的法学硕士回答了每个问题。多项选择和代码回答会自动评分，判断和情景回答则由法学硕士法官进行评分，其分数将与来自另一个模型系列的第二名法官和人工重新评分进行核对。综合得分范围为 54.4% 至 83.6%。每种任务类型的最高分是多项选择98.6%，代码95.1%，场景诊断88.4%，但判断只有58.8%。在各个模型中，88.5% 的判决是正确的，但其理由仅获得 53.4% 的评分。多项选择已接近最强模型的上限，并且大多数代码任务都已解决，而证明安全判决的合理性仍然是最弱的能力。基准、提示和每个项目的结果都是公开的。
papers.abstractEn: For Internet of Things (IoT) devices, a secure algorithm alone is not enough: an attacker with physical access can attack the implementation directly, and its flaws are hard to fix once deployed. Large language models (LLMs) are now used to build and analyze such implementations. LLM benchmarks exist for cryptography and general cybersecurity, but none covers cryptographic engineering. In this paper, we present CESBench, 380 expert-written items across six sub-domains of cryptographic engineering security for IoT devices: side-channel, fault injection, implementation, countermeasures, evaluation, and integration. Four task types target different competences: 209 multiple-choice items test recall, 67 judgment items require a security verdict and its justification, 63 scenario items require an engineering diagnosis, and 41 code tasks are graded by 572 test cases. To validate the benchmark, 11 open-weight and proprietary LLMs answer every item. Multiple-choice and code responses are scored automatically, and judgment and scenario responses by an LLM judge, whose scores are checked against a second judge from another model family and human re-scoring. Composite scores range from 54.4% to 83.6%. The top score on each task type is 98.6% for multiple choice, 95.1% for code, and 88.4% for scenario diagnosis, but only 58.8% for judgment. Across models, 88.5% of verdicts are correct, yet their justifications earn only 53.4% of the rubric marks. Multiple choice is near its ceiling for the strongest models and most code tasks are solved, whereas justifying a security verdict remains the weakest competence. The benchmark, prompts, and per-item results are public.

papers.title: Large Language Models as Falsifiers for Cyber-Physical Systems
papers.abstract: 证伪在网络物理系统（CPS）中寻找正式规范的反例。通过用信号时态逻辑 (STL) 编写的规范，伪造可以被表述为鲁棒性优化问题，传统上通过黑盒搜索算法来解决。与此同时，大型语言模型（LLM）最近在与迭代提示相结合时成为令人惊讶的有效优化器。在这项工作中，我们将这些想法联系起来，并引入了 LLM-Falsifier，这是一种基于 LLM 的方法，通过最小化 STL 的鲁棒性程度来伪造规范。除了基于通用提示的优化之外，我们的关键思想是将 LLM 暴露给语言模型自然但标准数值优化器所缺少的语义信息，包括自然语言输入和输出名称、输出轨迹以及最小鲁棒性值的关键时间见证。这些新增功能可实现更智能、样本效率更高的鲁棒性搜索。在 ARCH-COMP 证伪基准上，根据找到反例所需的平均模拟次数来衡量，LLM-Falsifier 在 21 个规范中的 14 个规范中，表现优于基于一系列优化范式（从基于代理和贝叶斯优化到基于搜索的测试）的现有证伪工具。
papers.abstractEn: Falsification searches for counterexamples to formal specifications in cyber-physical systems (CPS). With specifications written in Signal Temporal Logic (STL), falsification can be formulated as a robustness optimization problem, traditionally tackled with black-box search algorithms. In parallel, large language models (LLMs) have recently emerged as surprisingly effective optimizers when coupled with iterative prompting. In this work, we connect these ideas and introduce LLM-Falsifier, an LLM-based approach that falsifies specifications by minimizing the STL robustness degree. Beyond generic prompt-based optimization, our key idea is to expose the LLM to semantic information that is natural for language models but absent from standard numerical optimizers, including natural-language input and output names, output trajectories, and critical-time witnesses for the minimum robustness value. These additions enable smarter and more sample-efficient robustness search. On the ARCH-COMP falsification benchmarks, LLM-Falsifier is shown to outperform existing falsification tools based on a range of optimization paradigms, from surrogate-based and Bayesian optimization to search-based testing, on 14 of 21 specifications when measured by the average number of simulations required to find a counterexample.

papers.title: PoVD: Efficient Consensus Protocol based on Verifiable Delay Function
papers.abstract: 共识协议确保区块链和基于其构建的去中心化应用程序的稳健性和可扩展性。然而，现有的共识机制通常会带来较高的计算成本或需要大量的通信开销。为了应对这些挑战，我们提出了可验证延迟证明（PoVD），这是一种基于可验证延迟函数（VDF）的轻量级共识协议。我们给出了 PoVD 的详细协议，包括区块挖掘和验证规则，并说明了 PoVD 如何根据网络状况灵活调整区块时间分布。通过数学证明，我们指出，在网络相对较弱的假设下，PoVD 在保持相同吞吐量的情况下可以实现比 PoW 更低的分叉率。我们的实验验证了PoVD具有较低的计算和通信复杂度，还可以提高区块链的一致性，使其特别适合资源受限的节点和带宽有限的网络。
papers.abstractEn: Consensus protocols ensure the robustness and scalability of blockchains and decentralized applications built on them. However, existing consensus mechanisms often impose high computational cost or require heavy communication overhead. To address these challenges, we propose proof of verifiable delay (PoVD), a lightweight consensus protocol based on the verifiable delay function (VDF). We present the detailed protocol of PoVD, including the block mining and verification rules, and illustrate how PoVD can flexibly adjust the block time distribution according to the network condition. Through mathematical proof, we point out that, under a relatively weak network assumption, PoVD can achieve a lower fork rate than PoW while maintaining the same throughput. Our experiments verify that PoVD exhibits low computation and communication complexity and can also improve the blockchain consistency, making it particularly suitable for resource-constrained nodes and bandwidth-limited networks.

papers.title: AUPE: Collaborative byzantine fault-tolerant peer-sampling
papers.abstract: 对等采样是分布式系统中的关键原语，用于在大规模场景（例如无需许可的区块链系统）中管理覆盖和传播信息。其目的是维护并定期更新整个系统成员资格的本地和部分快照或视图。这些协议通常是恶意行为者的目标，他们的目的是破坏更高级别的协议。通常，控制一组拜占庭节点的对手试图通过增加合法节点在诚实节点看来的代表性来操纵合法节点如何感知拜占庭节点的存在。虽然最先进的拜占庭容忍对等采样协议可以减轻这种偏差，但随着恶意节点数量的增加，其有效性显着下降。本文介绍了 AUPE，这是第一个协作拜占庭容忍的对等采样协议，它利用可信节点（例如支持 SGX 的英特尔设备）的存在来协作跟踪系统中标识符的传播，并在本地消除拜占庭节点表示的偏差。 10,000 个节点的模拟表明，AUPE 的性能优于最先进的解决方案，即使面对控制 26% 节点的对手，也能实现近乎完美的弹性。总体而言，通过包含少至 10% 的可信节点，AUPE 将 BRAHMS 的容忍度提高了多达 60%，同时限制了对手攻击的影响，即使在拥有多达 40% 的节点时也是如此。
papers.abstractEn: Peer sampling is a crucial primitive in distributed systems, used to manage overlays and disseminate information in large-scale scenarios such as permissionless blockchain systems. Its purpose is to maintain and regularly update a local and partial snapshot, or view, of the complete system's membership. These protocols are often targeted by malicious actors who aim to disrupt higher-level protocols. Typically, an adversary who controls a set of byzantine nodes attempts to manipulate how legitimate nodes perceive the presence of byzantine ones by increasing their representation in the view of honest nodes. While state-of-the-art byzantine-tolerant peer sampling protocols mitigate this bias, their effectiveness decreases significantly as the number of malicious nodes increases. This paper introduces AUPE, the first collaborative Byzantine-tolerant peer sampling protocol that leverages the presence of trusted nodes, such as Intel's SGX capable devices, to collaboratively track the spread of identifiers in the system and locally debias the representation of byzantine nodes. Simulations with 10,000 nodes demonstrate that AUPE outperforms state-of-the-art solutions, achieving nearperfect resilience even when faced with an adversary controlling 26% of the nodes. Overall, by including as few as 10% of trusted nodes, AUPE increases the tolerance of BRAHMS by up to 60% while limiting the impact of the adversary's attack, even when possessing up to 40% of the nodes.
